loze / Entity / Particular / Schematic Particular

Schematic Particular

Class

A particular that is not bounded to one spatial location at a time and that can be concretized by concrete particulars

https://loze-ontology.org/SchematicParticular
ttlrdfjsonldnt
In short

A schematic particular sits between an instance and a class. It repeats like a class — many things can be concretizations of it — but it carries data like an instance, and it can be an eventuality as much as a thing. That is what lets you say something general about it using the same triples you would use for any individual. Without it, saying the same thing needs OWL 2 punning or a restriction.

For example

A document (as opposed to its particular copies), a work of music (as opposed to its performances), an alphabetic character (as opposed to its inscriptions), a software (as opposed to its installed copies), a substance or material like water or gold (as opposed to their circumscribed portions), a car model (as opposed to its units)

Note

Similarly to classes, schematic particulars are not bounded to one particular location at a time: as a rule, a schematic particular is wholly present wherever one of its concretizations is present; War and Peace is present wherever one of its copies is present; water is present wherever one or more H2O molecules are present; the Toyota Corolla is present wherever one of its units is present

loze is a top-level ontology after E. J. Lowe's four-category ontology, with Zemach's schematic particulars. Every term here is identified by an IRI under https://loze-ontology.org/.
